page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc7.32xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal instance powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processors operating at a nominal clock speed of 2.9 GHz. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The bare metal architecture bypasses virtualization overhead, granting workloads direct physical access to compute resources.

Network interfaces deliver a baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps, facilitating high-throughput node-to-node communication. The instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring persistent data to be attached via external block storage volumes or remote networked storage solutions. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs configured on this platform.

With its compute-heavy resource profile, this instance provides high density for CPU-intensive processing tasks. Architectural tradeoffs center on the lack of built-in storage and moderate memory capacity relative to core count. The instance is suited for compute-bound operations, including high-concurrency batch processing, scientific simulations, video transcoding pipelines, large-scale distributed compilation, and front-tier container nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc7.32xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal instance engineered for compute-heavy enterprise workloads. It is powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processors clocked at 2.9 GHz, delivering 128 dedicated physical cores alongside 256 GB of memory, which establishes a 1:2 core-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Operating directly on bare-metal hardware without virtualization overhead, the system supports low-latency execution and high compute density. Network connectivity is rated at a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth, offering throughput for distributed clustered environments. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating cloud block storage integration for disk-dependent tasks. With its extensive core density and fast network pipe, ecs.ebmc7.32xlarge is targeted toward parallel computing tasks, distributed compilation, video encoding pipelines, batch execution workloads, and high-performance continuous integration environments.
